our_side_1600.verdict: the mamba page size is a property of the GDN state layout only (conv (10240, 3+num_spec) bf16 + recurrent (48,128,128) fp32). It is not a property of MambaSpec, not of mamba_cache_mode, and not of any allocator. The inflation of the ATTENTION block is entirely the platform's single-page-size unification in _align_hybrid_block_size

is_the_coupling_genuine.answer: NO. Per-cache-group page geometry is already implemented and shipped in this image.

mechanism.note: prepare_kernel_block_sizes returns ONE kernel block size PER KV cache group; AttentionSpec groups get select_common_block_size(storage, backends); MambaSpec groups get kv_cache_spec.block_size unchanged
select_common_block_size: case 2 walks int-format supported sizes descending and returns the first that divides the storage block. 1600 % 64 == 0 -> 64
BlockTable sets use_hybrid_blocks and blocks_per_kv_block = block_size // kernel_block_size
get_kv_cache_shape is called with shape_block_size = kernel_block_size, and num_blocks *= block_size // kernel_block_size

upstream_provenance.pr: vllm-project/vllm#24486 '[Hybrid]: Decouple Kernel Block Size from KV Page Size', zhiyuan1i, MERGED 2025-10-09
upstream_provenance.verbatim: This PR introduces a hybrid cache architecture that separates logical kernel block size from physical page size... This hybrid model decoupling enables independent development of high-performance operators without being constrained by linear attention mechanisms like Mamba
upstream_provenance.motivating_issue: vllm-project/vllm#24280, tomeras91, opened 2025-09-04, CLOSED as completed 2025-10-09
upstream_provenance.issue_verbatim: in hybrid mamba/attention models the KVCacheManager requires the mamba and attention page sizes to match, which might cause large attention page sizes (672 tokens for nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2)... If the KVCacheManager requires a page size larger than what is supported by the attention backend, we can create multiple pages for the attention backend from a single KVCacheManager page.
upstream_provenance.closing_confirmation: Thanks @zhiyuan1i for merging https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/24486 :) I can confirm this solves the issue for nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2

scale_of_the_cost.reading: the FP8 prefill path costs 4.4x the entire published quantization error of the artifact. Speed here does not merely cost quality; it erases the artifact's reason to exist.

does_a_weights_only_variant_escape_it.candidate: reconstruct_fp8dg_nt - vendor, built into the baked .so, zero callers anywhere in the image, FP8 weights into DeepGEMM NT layout with one FP32 scale per 128x128 tile
does_a_weights_only_variant_escape_it.why_it_does_not_escape: every FP8 weight consumer on this stack is FP8 x FP8: DeepGEMM's NT entry and torch._scaled_mm both require an FP8 A operand. So an FP8 weight operand forces FP8 activations, which is exactly where PR #318 attributes the loss. The only thing reconstruct_fp8dg_nt changes is WEIGHT scale granularity (per-128x128 tile instead of per-output-channel), and weight granularity is already ruled out as the cause: per-tensor cost +0.0139 and per-output-channel cost +0.0141, i.e. finer weight scaling did not help.
does_a_weights_only_variant_escape_it.verdict: [INFERENCE] very unlikely to change the verdict; ranked as a cheap disproof, not a lever
does_a_weights_only_variant_escape_it.deep_gemm_present: deep_gemm 2.5.0+a6b593d is installed in the same venv

vendor_claim.verbatim: Fused path: reconstruct emits ORIGINAL-basis weights (both Hadamards + sign vectors folded into the memory-bound reconstruct kernel), so the gemm runs on the raw input and the standalone input/output had_r_128 launches disappear (~14% of long-chunk prefill GPU time)... The fused kernel costs ~4x plain reconstruct (k*n-proportional) while the saved had launches scale with rows*(k+n); breakeven is rows ~400-900 across shapes
vendor_claim.gate: use_fused = self._fused_reconstruct and rows >= 1024, both dims 128-divisible
vendor_claim.release: turboderp-org/exllamav3 v1.4.0, 2026-08-06, release notes 'Faster prefill (all models)'; commit d33be5ce, 2026-08-03

sources: docs/26-prefill-attribution.md ('At m=2048 a gate_proj shape costs 1.20 ms end to end of which the GEMM is 0.90 ms; the remaining ~0.30 ms is Hadamard + reconstruct')
receipts/v3-prefill-micro.json reconstruct_ms for mlp.gate_proj K=5120 N=17408 bits=5

our_arithmetic.verdict: [INFERENCE] the vendor's ~14% does NOT transfer to our shapes at our chunk size. At m=2048 the fused kernel is predicted to cost 1.31x the unfused path on gate_proj: it removes 0.133 ms of Hadamard and adds 0.502 ms of reconstruct. Breakeven is around 7,600 rows for gate/up and down, and only the tiny k_proj/v_proj (breakeven ~1,600 rows) would win at 2048. Our max_num_batched_tokens is 2048.
our_arithmetic.caveat: the 0.133 ms Hadamard figure is a subtraction from two independently measured quantities, not a direct measurement; a 10-minute microbench settles it

ranked_work_items.title: Enable per-batch-size (or acceptance-adaptive) speculative depth at FULL_DECODE_ONLY by opting into the V2 model runner
ranked_work_items.build_or_fix: set VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 and speculative_config.num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size (e.g. [(1,4,3),(5,8,1)] style triples) instead of a fixed num_speculative_tokens=3
files: /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vllm/config/vllm.py:640-666 (_is_default_v2_model_runner_model returns False for is_hybrid, which is why we default to V1)
/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py:70-91 (draft-decode manager rejects PIECEWISE and upgrades to FULL_DECODE_ONLY)
/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py:215-276 (one FULL uniform-decode graph per draft depth, with a K=0 guard)
ranked_work_items.estimated_effect: +25 to +31% aggregate decode throughput at concurrency 8, with no loss at C1
ranked_work_items.effect_basis: MEASURED, receipts/perf-sweep-5090.json: num_speculative_tokens=1 at C8 gives 409.35 tok/s against 313.28 for MTP-3, i.e. +30.7%, while MTP-3 is what wins at C1 (82.94 tok/s). A per-batch-size schedule takes both instead of choosing. The [INFERENCE] part is only that the switch is free of overhead.
ranked_work_items.measurement: re-run the perf-sweep decode rows at C1/C4/C8 with the schedule and confirm C1 >= 82.9 and C8 >= 400 tok/s in one server; check the startup log for 'Overriding cudagraph_mode ... to PIECEWISE' being ABSENT and for the EXL3 graph-decode info line naming FULL_DECODE_ONLY
ranked_work_items.what_could_break: (1) if VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER is not set, vLLM silently rewrites the mode to PIECEWISE at config time and Exl3Config._require_enforce_eager then raises 'The EXL3 quantization backend requires eager execution' - a loud failure, not a silent regression. (2) V2 runner + hybrid mamba + MTP + EXL3 + fp8 KV is a combination we have never run; V2 owns its own KV/mamba state plumbing, so re-verify context capacity and the GDN gate behaviour. (3) local-inference-lab/vllm#298 (open) warns that a prompt chunk carrying K+1 tokens per request can let a decode FULL graph replay over prompt state, producing valid-looking garbage - re-run the fidelity guard, not just the throughput rows.
ranked_work_items.provenance: upstream cover: vllm-project/vllm#45953 '[MRV2][SD] Make Dynamic SD comatible with Full Cuda Graphs', ekagra-ranjan, MERGED 2026-07-04

ranked_work_items.title: Widen _b12x_trellis_k6_supported from K6-only to every MCG bitrate b12x accepts
ranked_work_items.kind: one-line vLLM change, gated behind a microbenchmark
ranked_work_items.build_or_fix: change exl3.py:1215 from int(trellis.shape[2]) == 96 to int(trellis.shape[2]) in (32,48,64,80,96) (bits 2-6). This is the clause - and the ONLY clause - that rejects all 208 attention projections and both MLP gate/up families: they are mcg, int16, ndim 3, and 128-divisible on both axes
files: /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/b12x/moe/_shared/kernels/w4a16/prepare.py:2082-2087 (dense prepare accepts the same bit range)
ranked_work_items.estimated_effect: UNKNOWN SIGN. Possibly large at decode, possibly a regression.
ranked_work_items.effect_basis: the upside basis is MEASURED but only for K6: exl3.py:1275-1276 'measured on SM120 it beats reconstruct+GEMM by ~5x at m=1-8'. The catch is [INFERENCE] and structural: _use_k6_mcg_small hard-requires trellis_bits == 6, so K5 shards admitted by the widened gate would run the GENERIC CuTe trellis256 scheduler, not the tuned small-M CUDA kernel. There is no measurement anywhere of the generic scheduler at m in {1..32} against ext.exl3_gemm on a K5 shape. It could easily be slower.
ranked_work_items.measurement: extend tools/b12x_vs_reconstruct.py with a K5 arm and a small-m sweep: b12x trellis_linear.run vs ext.exl3_gemm at m in {1,4,8,16,32,128} on the four real K5 geometries (5120x17408, 5120x10240, 5120x6144, 6144x5120) and on 5120x12288. Roughly 5 GPU-minutes, no serving run. Only widen the gate if b12x wins at 4, 16 and 32 rows, which are C1/C4/C8 with MTP-3.
ranked_work_items.what_could_break: the 343 K5/K4 shards currently run the bit-faithful ext.exl3_gemm; moving them to b12x changes the arithmetic and must be re-qualified against the decode-parity captures (receipts/decode-parity-*.json), not just benchmarked. Also: the pre-capture priming pass at exl3.py:1090-1169 primes exl3_gemm; shards that move to b12x need b12x's own warm-then-capture instead, or graph capture will resolve a new CuTe kernel inside capture.
ranked_work_items.provenance: upstream cover for the premise that the bitrate limit is arbitrary: local-inference-lab/vllm PR #297 'feat(exl3): extend rank-sliced bitrate to accept K2' (open, 2026-08-12) - 'The b12x PTX dequant kernel is parametric in bits - shifts are bits, 2*bits, 3*bits with MCG/MASK/OR constants that are K-independent. All restrictions were Python-level validation guards, not compiled PTX limitations.' No upstream issue or PR has ever proposed widening this particular clause: genuinely undiscussed.

ranked_work_items.title: Bump the b12x wheel from 1.2.1 to 1.2.4 for the fused K6/MCG CuTe projection specialization
ranked_work_items.build_or_fix: rebuild the serving image against b12x master (1.2.3/tag 1.2.4), which contains b12x PR #221's gemm/trellis_linear/_k6_mcg_cute.py - absent from our install
ranked_work_items.estimated_effect: at most about 1.15x decode step time at C1 and C4; nothing at C8; nothing at prefill
ranked_work_items.effect_basis: VENDOR CLAIM: rtx6kpro#73 and b12x PR #221 report '2.0x to 6.4x faster' than the generic separate-H128 scheduler across 15 projection shapes, with E2E parity to +2.05% prefill. The ceiling is ours to compute [INFERENCE]: the specialization covers unpaired MCG K6 at 1-16 rows only, which is our 66 K6 matrices at C1 (4 rows) and C4 (16 rows) but not C8 (32 rows). Those 66 matrices carry 7.065 of the 26.047 GMAC/token of linear work (27.1%), so even a 2x kernel win bounds the whole-step improvement at 1.16x, and less than that because decode is weight-bandwidth bound rather than MAC bound.
ranked_work_items.measurement: decode rows at C1/C4/C8 before and after the image bump, plus the b12x_vs_reconstruct microbench at m in {1,4,8,16} on 17408x5120 K6
ranked_work_items.what_could_break: a whole-image bump moves every other b12x kernel at the same time, so any decode regression is hard to attribute. b12x master also carries the pre-cute-rebase-20260807 boundary. And the specialization does not cover C8, so the bump can help C1/C4 while doing nothing for the concurrency we actually serve at.

ranked_work_items.title: Make B12X_ATTN loadable on a hybrid model: relax the three b12x-local page-size gates
ranked_work_items.kind: about 12 lines of vLLM, no kernel change
ranked_work_items.build_or_fix: (G-A) delete or modulo-ise supports_block_size at b12x_attn.py:417-418; (G-B) stop validating cache_config.block_size at b12x_attn.py:690-696 and use the negotiated kernel page the builder already receives; (G-C) fix _max_page_table_width at b12x_attn.py:85-97 to reserve cdiv(L, storage) * (storage // kernel_page)
ranked_work_items.estimated_effect: bounded above by about 10% of prefill and an unknown decode delta; realistically small
ranked_work_items.effect_basis: MEASURED bound: docs/26-prefill-attribution.md arms A->C and B->D put the whole attention representation at 1.05x-1.11x of prefill. [INFERENCE] for the rest: at head_dim 256 b12x caps the prefill query tile at 64 (planner.py:698-704, byte-faithful to flashinfer utils.cuh:412) and _paged_is_invalid (traits.py:83-100) independently forbids cta_tile_q=128, so we would pay 2x the CTA count of a head_dim-128 model; and every SM120 analytic decode/verify family requires head_dim 128, so we would land on the generic paths. Our 24q/4kv/gqa6 head counts match those families exactly and miss only on head_dim.
ranked_work_items.measurement: start the server with --attention-backend B12X_ATTN after the three edits and check the startup log reports a kernel page of 64 (select_common_block_size(1600,[b12x]) = 64 because 1600 % 128 != 0), then run the existing prefill and decode sweep rows against the FLASHINFER baseline. A failure to reach 4,100 page-table entries reproduces b12x issue #29 and validates the G-C fix independently.
ranked_work_items.what_could_break: b12x issue #29 (open since 2026-07-11, zero comments) is the unpatched page-table overflow this item must fix, and it manifests only 'on first use with MTP'. mamba_cache_mode=align masks the shortfall via b12x_attn.py:92-96, so a fix validated in align mode is not validated in general. Also B12X_ATTN advertises AttentionCGSupport.UNIFORM_BATCH (b12x_attn.py:559), which resolve_cudagraph_mode_and_sizes turns into FULL_AND_PIECEWISE - and EXL3 refuses that mode, so this item collides with W1 unless the mode is pinned to FULL_DECODE_ONLY explicitly.
ranked_work_items.provenance: the capability is already shipped: vllm-project/vllm#24486 (MERGED 2025-10-09). The deletion has direct precedent in vllm-project/vllm#36701 (tdoublep, MERGED 2026-06-26), which removed FlashAttention's analogous hybrid-model block-size restriction. NOTE: the TODO(tdoublep) at platforms/interface.py:886 is NOT about this coupling - it is scoped to mamba chunk alignment in mamba_cache_mode='all', its PR is vllm-project/vllm#33194 (still open), and we run 'align', so it would not affect us.

ranked_work_items.title: Wire exllamav3's fused reconstruct_had_slice into the vLLM prefill path
ranked_work_items.kind: about 25 lines of vLLM plus a loader env var; the extension is already built
ranked_work_items.build_or_fix: mirror upstream exllamav3/modules/quant/exl3.py:171-215 inside _reconstruct_hgemm_into: when both dims are 128-divisible and rows are above a measured threshold, call ext.reconstruct_had_slice(w, trellis, suh, svh[n_start:], K, mcg, mul1, n_start) and skip both had_r_128 launches. Serve with VLLM_EXL3_EXT_PATH=/work/torch-ext/exllamav3_ext, which already exports the symbol
ranked_work_items.estimated_effect: predicted NEGATIVE at our chunk size: about 1.31x the current cost on gate_proj at m=2048
ranked_work_items.effect_basis: VENDOR CLAIM ~14% of long-chunk prefill GPU time, with the vendor's own caveat that the fused kernel 'costs ~4x plain reconstruct' and 'breakeven is rows ~400-900 across shapes'. [INFERENCE] with measured inputs: at m=2048 gate_proj is 1.20 ms total = 0.90 GEMM + 0.167 reconstruct + 0.133 for both had launches (docs/26 plus receipts/v3-prefill-micro.json). Fused predicts 0.90 + 4x0.167 = 1.57 ms. Per element, had costs 2.88 ps and reconstruct 1.88 ps, a ratio of 1.53, which puts breakeven at about 7,750 rows for gate/up and down and about 1,670 rows for k_proj/v_proj. Our max_num_batched_tokens is 2048, so only the two tiny projections win.
ranked_work_items.measurement: microbenchmark, no serving run, about 10 GPU-minutes: for each of 5120x17408 (K5), 17408x5120 (K6), 5120x248320 (K6), 5120x1024 (K5), time had_r_128 + reconstruct_slice + hgemm + had_r_128 against reconstruct_had_slice + hgemm at m in {512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192} using /work/torch-ext/exllamav3_ext. This also directly measures the 0.133 ms Hadamard figure that is currently a subtraction.
ranked_work_items.what_could_break: nothing in serving if the microbench says no - the item dies cheaply. If it says yes for some shapes, the threshold must be per-geometry, and it must live INSIDE the custom op for the same Dynamo reason documented at exl3.py:761-765 (a Python-level row test bakes the prefill branch into the decode graphs: measured 56.5 -> 22.6 tok/s at C1). Fidelity: upstream's own tolerance for the fused kernel is errs/scale < 2e-3 (tests/test_reconstruct_had.py:67), i.e. fp16, not bit-exact, so the decode-parity captures still apply.
ranked_work_items.provenance: turboderp-org/exllamav3 commit d33be5ce (2026-08-03), released in v1.4.0 (2026-08-06) whose notes read 'Faster prefill (all models)'

ranked_work_items.title: Disprove (or salvage) the weights-only FP8 prefill variant using the already-built reconstruct_fp8dg_nt
ranked_work_items.kind: one microbenchmark; an experiment, not a feature
ranked_work_items.build_or_fix: call the baked extension's reconstruct_fp8dg_nt (FP8 weights into DeepGEMM NT layout, one FP32 scale per 128x128 tile) against deep_gemm 2.5.0 and measure both speed and KLD on one layer
ranked_work_items.estimated_effect: expected to reproduce roughly the same +0.0141-class KLD penalty as VLLM_EXL3_PREFILL_FP8, for a similar prefill gain
ranked_work_items.effect_basis: [INFERENCE], and the reasoning is why this is ranked low rather than high: DeepGEMM NT and torch._scaled_mm are both FP8 x FP8, so an FP8 weight operand forces FP8 activations, and PR #318 attributes the loss to the activations, not the weights. Weight-scale granularity is already ruled out as the cause: per-tensor cost +0.0139 (exl3.py:826-831) and per-output-channel cost +0.0141 - refining the weight scaling did not help, so refining it further to per-128x128 tile should not either.
ranked_work_items.measurement: one-layer teacher-forced KLD on the existing fidelity suite plus a GEMM microbench; kill the item if mean KLD exceeds the published 0.00321 by more than a factor of two
ranked_work_items.what_could_break: nothing - it is a read-only experiment. Its value is closing the last FP8 door with evidence instead of inference.

ranked_work_items.title: VLLM_EXL3_PREFILL_FP8
ranked_work_items.build_or_fix: nothing. The extension at /work/torch-ext/exllamav3_ext already exports reconstruct_fp8_slice, so this flag can be made live TODAY with one env var and no build - and it should not be
ranked_work_items.estimated_effect: +31% prefill (MEASURED, ours, PR #318) for +0.0141 mean KLD (MEASURED, ours, PR #318)
ranked_work_items.effect_basis: the cost is 4.4x the artifact's entire published mean KLD of 0.00321 (receipts/kld5-10M-k5k6.json, 10,480,640 scored positions). The whole point of this checkpoint family is fidelity per byte; +0.0141 puts it behind official FP8, which is the comparison it exists to win.
ranked_work_items.measurement: already measured. Do not re-measure; do re-label the '1.5-1.8x' number wherever it appears as an isolated-GEMM microbenchmark

ranked_work_items.title: The only remaining real prefill lever is a fused dequant-in-GEMM-epilogue kernel
ranked_work_items.build_or_fix: a Marlin-style kernel that dequantizes the trellis inside the GEMM epilogue, so the weight is never materialized
ranked_work_items.estimated_effect: the arithmetic ceiling is 11.8k tok/s MLP-only, i.e. roughly 7-8k end to end, against 5.6k measured on an RTX PRO 6000 and 3,374 on our 5090
ranked_work_items.effect_basis: MEASURED and published: docs/26-prefill-attribution.md - ext.hgemm is at cuBLAS parity (0.92-1.06x) so there is no free GEMM win; a perfect fused kernel that made reconstruct free gives 64 x 2.70 ms = 173 ms. Maintainer statement, local-inference-lab/vllm PR #316 comment 5299700465, 2026-08-15: 'prefill parity with FP8 is not reachable for a 4-bit-class trellis format by dispatch or tuning changes in this runtime. It needs dequant fused into the GEMM epilogue (Marlin-style) - a new kernel, out of scope for this PR.'
ranked_work_items.what_could_break: n/a - listed so the ranked list is honest about where the headroom actually is

could_not_determine_without_running_it: Whether the promoted serving image localhost/vllm:gg-r34-patched-apc (manifest sha256:16a936b8...) carries the same /opt/exllamav3-python source tree and the same baked extension as the pinned base rootfs. Neither podman nor docker nor skopeo is installed on this host and I had no GPU window, so I could only read the base image voipmonitor/vllm@sha256:820181fb... via its flattened rootfs and file manifest.

Every performance number attributed to a work item is either a re-quotation of an existing receipt or an inference from one. Nothing in this document was measured during this ticket: the RTX 5090 was held by KvDtypeSweep throughout.

The absolute milliseconds in receipts/b12x-vs-reconstruct.json carry no device field. Their output path (/work/kld3) places them in the iteration-3 series, which docs/26 documents as one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, so the ratios are the transferable part and the absolute times are not the 5090's.

Whether the generic CuTe trellis256 scheduler beats ext.exl3_gemm on a K5 shape at 4/16/32 rows. This is the whole sign of work item W2 and it needs 5 GPU-minutes to settle; no measurement of it exists anywhere.

Whether the V2 model runner actually serves this hybrid VL model correctly. Nothing in _get_v2_model_runner_unsupported_features rejects it, but 'not rejected at config time' is not 'known to work', and we have never run V2 on this checkpoint.

The 0.133 ms two-launch Hadamard cost underpinning the W5 refutation is a subtraction of two independently measured quantities (docs/26's 1.20/0.90 ms and v3-prefill-micro's 0.167 ms), not a direct measurement.
